questions.question: Construct a DFA for L = {w ∈ {0,1}* : w contains '11' as a substring}.
questions.solutionApproach: States: q0 (start, no progress), q1 (just saw one '1'), q2 (accepting, saw '11'). q0 on 1→q1, on 0→q0. q1 on 1→q2, on 0→q0. q2 on 0 or 1→q2 (stays accepting once found).
questions.answer: 3-state DFA: q0→q1 on '1', q1→q2 on '1' (accept), q2 stays on any input; both q0,q1 go back to q0 on '0'.

questions.question: A DFA has states {q0,q1}, accepting={q1}, but has NO transition defined from q1 on symbol 'b'. If you swap accepting/non-accepting to find the complement, is this correct?
questions.solutionApproach: No — the DFA is INCOMPLETE (missing q1 on 'b'). Must first add a trap/dead state to handle the missing transition (making it a complete DFA), THEN swap accept/reject. Naive swapping on an incomplete DFA gives a wrong complement.
questions.answer: No — must complete the DFA (add trap state) before complementing.

questions.question: An NFA has states {q0,q1,q2}; from q0 on '0' it can go to {q0,q1}; from q1 on '1' it goes to {q2}; q2 is accepting. Does the NFA accept '01'?
questions.solutionApproach: Track possible-state sets: start {q0}. After '0': {q0,q1} (both reachable). After '1': from q0 on '1' — no transition defined (dead); from q1 on '1' — {q2}. Combined set: {q2}. q2 is accepting → ACCEPT.
questions.answer: Yes, accepted — reaches q2 via the q0→q1→q2 path.

questions.question: A DFA has 2 states: q0(start,accepting) and q1. On '0', q0→q1 and q1→q0. On '1', both states self-loop. What language does it accept?
questions.solutionApproach: State tracks parity of '0' count. q0 = even count of 0's seen (accepting), q1 = odd. '1's don't affect state. Language = strings with an EVEN number of 0's.
questions.answer: {w : number of 0's in w is even}
